recipes.name: Apple-Stuffed Acorn Squash
ingredients_raw: 3 cups peeled, seeded, and chopped Granny Smith apples

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place squash halves, cut-sides down, onto a baking sheet. Add enough water to come ½ inch up sides of the baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 40 minutes. Drain off any remaining water.
Meanwhile, melt margarine in a large skillet over medium heat. Add apples and onions; cook until onions softened and turned translucent, 10 to 15 minutes. Transfer mixture to a bowl to cool.
When squash is cooked, stir Cheddar cheese, raisins, brown sugar, and cinnamon into apple mixture until evenly combined. Flip squash halves on the baking sheet; fill cavities with apple mixture.
Bake in the heated oven until filling is hot and cheese is melted, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple-Stuffed Acorn Squash
raw_recipe.description: In this vegetarian recipe for apple-stuffed acorn squash, Granny Smith apples and Cheddar cheese combine to make a delicious filling for squash halves.

review.reviewBody: My family was delighted with the squash! I made a few changes in technique. I salted the squash, as another reviewer suggested and also flipped the squash, so that the acorn "bowl" was in the water. I soaked the raisins in 1/2 cup of hot apple juice and then added the apple juice to the apple mixture. Also, I scooped the squash from the acorn and added it to the apple mixture. It was delicious. My brother was literally scraping his acorn "bowl".

This recipe provides a lovely combination of savory and sweet flavors. Substitutions I made include: 1) Butter, instead of oleomargarine (yuck!); 2) Walla walla sweet onion instead of "onion"; 3) Canadian - 100% natural-pure maple syrup instead of "light brown sugar"; 4) added 1/2 teaspoon of allspice along with the 1 teaspoon of cinnamon; 5) Added 1/2 cup of chopped pecans. Result: a lovely, sweet and savory desert that can be either side dish or dessert! Your original recipe is a four star version. I think my version is five star. To each, his or her own, I suppose.

This is delicious and very versatile! I used half the brown sugar, and cranberries instead of raisins, which I soaked in about 2 tablespoons of hot apple cider while the squash was cooking, and then added all of it to the stuffing. I also salted the squash bowls lightly before stuffing. For final prep, scrapped the squash out, chopped it up a bit and mixed it in with the stuffing. The squash absorbed the apple cider, and it made a wonderful fall dinner. I did salt and pepper quite a bit while eating though, so the next time I plan on adding a little more salt, and maybe a dash of chipotle pepper or some other spicy seasoning to give it more of a savory, hot sweet taste.

This was okay, but a little plain on the first try. The 2nd time, I added some seasoning salt and fresh cracked pepper to the squash generously before filling with the onions, apples, etc. I also added Craisins since I had no golden raisins. I added a pinch of nutmeg, which I felt was a nice addition. Also, I changed the cheese to jack cheese - cheddar just didn't seem right to me. With the new additions, I received rave reviews. But, with these changes, it actually was quite tasty. I will make it again - with the changes, of course.

Will definitely make it again. Read through a lot of reviews first. Squash is a bland vegetable. I don’t understand the complaint, but I did salt my squash before adding the stuffing. I precooked my squash ( after clearing it) in the microwave. Sautéed the onions and apples and added some cinnamon. As someone suggested I added some cooked brown rice( the rice was cooked in apple juice) and dried cranberries to the apple mixture. Omitted the cheese and any other sugar. Before serving I put the squash in the microwave for 5 minutes on medium. The microwave works better/faster when cooking for one. If you make several, then the oven makes more sense. Will make this again . I can see adding pecans in the future.

I loved this. The only two changes I made were to scoop the cooked squash out of their bowls and add that to the cooked apple and onion mixture. I did this because I knew none of the other eaters would actually eat the squash if prepared as directed. I added about a half teaspoon of salt to the mix because I forgot to salt the squash when baking during the first part. All of the ingredients added to the overall taste, so I wouldn't eliminate anything. Served with roast pork, everyone loved it!

Wonderful recipe… everyone loved it… I only used 2 acorn squash and I used 1/2 and 1/2 butter and evoo… I also used craisins instead of raisins… I also followed the suggestion to scoop out the squash and place in a casserole if serving a lot of people… and I added the nutmeg which someone else suggested… all in all.. this will be a staple in my recipe box… I made both parts ahead of time(except for the cheese) as we had to drive a long way and wanted to just get there and bake it… worked out great…mixed the topping with the cheese… placed it on top of the squash and baked… everyone raved…

It was good. If I were making it again, I would caramelize the onions and cook the apples after. I'd also increase the raisins and bump up the spices with cinnamon, nutmeg, cardamom, or similar. You could make it non fat by leaving off the cheese and sautéing the onions in a little wine.

I loved it! I have to echo the hesitation about the cheddar cheese, but I used less than was suggested and it really just added to the consistency, though I didn't taste much in the flavor. I used dried cranberries and honey instead of the brown sugar. Scooped out the majority of the squash and mixed with the apple mixture, just for ease. Was very happy with the result, even my friend who really doesn't like cheese was happy with it. Yummy vegetarian meal!

Great starter for a recipe! I read comments and did a lot of substitutions as a result and because of what I had on hand and it was excellent. I salted the squash, used butter and sweet onions, honeycrisp apples, dates instead of raisins, and added pistachios and used sharp cheddar and it was super tasty, and almost better on re-heat. I pulled the squash out and mixed in as well for a nice balance and used a touch of all spice and cinnamon. Also, I made chicken with it and wish I'd just added the chicken into the mixture! Great recipe with loads of ways to adjust.

I love this recipe, but do yourself a favor and add quinoa to the mix! It adds dimension, protein, and it acts as a binding agent for the other fillers! I also add walnuts to mine and sub the raisins for craisins.

It’s sweet. I added salt and pepper. I like the comment below: “Also, I scooped the squash from the acorn and added it to the apple mixture.” When I do this recipe again, I will do that. Easier eating! 😋
This was great. Added to some quinoa

An interesting sweet and savory combination. Since other reviewers complained about the squash being bland, I brushed the squash halves with oil, salt and pepper and cooked cut side up. I also added salt, pepper, brown rice (cooked in chicken broth and butter) and pecans to the filling based on other reviews. Even so, we thought it didn't quite have that oomph we were looking for. Missing something to really bring it together but not sure what. The end result was decent, but didn't wow us enough to bother making again. Even though I added salt during cooking we both ended up adding more salt while eating.

I baked them in salt water as recommended and flipped them- I also added salt & pepper to sauté , soaked raisins in pan water - I made it all in advance and baked later - but cooking squash did take over a hour & I did add more butter in sauté to but I use plant based - super good I ate two halves -had no room for dessert

I love acorn squash but agree with a few others that something was missing. I added salt and pepper so that wasn't it, but I can't tell what it needed. I would describe this dish as "okay" but wouldn't make it again. As a side note, I thought the cheddar cheese would taste a bit odd in this dish, but it didn't. In fact, I couldn't even tell it was in there. I used a medium cheddar, but sharp might have been preferable. Thanks for sharing, though. I always appreciate trying a new recipe. (:
Tastes great! Not too difficult to make! I love it!
Ehhhh.
I addedchicken, 1 tsp nutmeg, and the apple juice soaked raisins. I also used maple syrup instead of brown sugar, and a tbsp of minced garlic instead of the onion. We loved it!
It's very easy and my family could not have loved it more. Takes a while to cook but it is worth it!
